title: Post-Quantum Bounds for Ascon and Keyed Sponges
summary: The current tweakable Even–Mansour reduction does not cover independent Ascon permutations; improved, ideally tight post-quantum bounds for Ascon and keyed sponges remain open.

formal_statement.body: Determine improved, ideally tight, post-quantum security bounds for Ascon and keyed sponge functions analyzed through a reduction to tweakable Even--Mansour. For Ascon, the existing reduction requires its two permutations, $p_a$ and $p_b$, to be modeled as a single random permutation and does not work when they are modeled as independent permutations. The new bounds should explicitly identify which permutation model they cover.

scope.domain: Post-quantum security analysis of Ascon and keyed sponge functions through reductions to tweakable Even–Mansour.
assumptions: The existing Ascon reduction models p_a and p_b as a single random permutation.
parameters: p_a and p_b: the two Ascon permutations whose shared or independent modeling determines whether the reduction applies
scope.unresolved_remainder: Obtain improved, ideally tight, post-quantum security bounds for Ascon and keyed sponge functions and identify the permutation model covered by each bound.

citations.label: Post-Quantum Security of Keyed Sponge-Based Constructions through a Modular Approach

progress.summary: The source presents a better, especially tight, security bound as important future work and identifies the inability of the current Ascon reduction to handle independently modeled permutations as a limitation.
citation_labels: Akinori Hosoyamada et al., Post-Quantum Security of Keyed Sponge-Based Constructions through a Modular Approach
